defects: Title collides with the black slab in mid-film frames: 'in Bewegung' is cut to 'in Bewegun' by a hard edge that looks unintended, so the headline is clipped.
In one transition frame the headline sits on top of the red disc and the hatched block, so black type lands on red and on stripes. Legibility collapses during the move.
The circle reads slightly taller than wide in several frames. Either the disc is non-uniformly scaled or the aspect ratio is wrong, and it shows on a pure geometric shape.
Large displacements between frames 1/6 s apart with no motion blur, so moves strobe and step instead of reading as weighted travel.
The change curve alternates (80 / 9 / 89 / 10 / 102): the piece moves in bursts and then sits nearly still for about a second each time. The holds read as dead air, not as considered rests.
The fine 45° hatch is at risk of moiré and shimmer when it moves and is compressed. Its edges are crisp but the pattern is too dense for the frame size.
The hairline background grid is barely visible. The device the film is named after hardly reads.
The end frame is just another rearrangement. Nothing locks up, and it doesn't rhyme with the opening composition.
gaps: Choreography is one move repeated: every 2 s all the blocks reshuffle to new grid slots at once and then hold. There's no overlap or follow-through, no lead element handing off to the next, and no build to a peak. Top studio work would stagger the elements, let one shape drive the others, and escalate in tempo toward a final lock-up.

Weight and spacing are generic. Moves are fast snaps with no blur and no anticipation or settle that you can see, so the black slabs and the red disc all feel equally weightless. Mass isn't differentiated (heavy slab vs light disc), and the type has no motion behaviour of its own.

Finish and concept are thin. Flat vector fills with no texture or light, a clipped and occluded headline, a near-invisible grid and a possibly squashed circle. 'Raster in Bewegung' is stated in the title but never made visible: the grid lines never move, flex or govern the cut, so the film reads as a template Swiss-poster shuffle, not an idea.
